_doc: WHAT THE GROUND'S CULLING GRID COSTS ON THE FIELD IT NOW COVERS (T-0466). `renderers/web/js/terrain.js` cut the ground on the literals 12 x 3, and those two numbers were a measurement of ONE box: 2,020 m east-west by 800 m north-south. The southern field (T-0464) makes the modelled box 2,020 x 4,920 m and the ground MESH, skirt and all, 7,340 x 10,240 m -- so the literals were cutting the long axis into three, a tile 1,640 m deep on the modelled box and 3,413 m deep on the mesh: a strip that reaches from the walker's feet to the far end of the world, intersects the frustum from anywhere on it, and can therefore never be culled. This file is the reading that replaced them with a rule. GENERATED by tools/measure_ground_tiling.mjs --json; --check holds the committed rule to it.
instrument: The same one tools/measure_detail_ceilings.mjs uses: the published mirror served over http, the real renderer booted on it, driven through the `__chicago4d` handle the gate drives, and `renderer.info` read as three.js itself counts it. The candidate is forced by rewriting the SERVED copy of js/terrain.js in flight, so one tree is read at several tilings and none of them is committed; `derived` is the unpatched rule. Every candidate gets its own page, because an ES module is cached per context.
what_this_is_not: NOT a ceiling reading. These numbers are a COMPARISON between tilings on one instrument in one sitting, and the four downtown figures sit above what tools/measure_detail_ceilings.mjs reports for the same stands, so the instrument is not calibrated against the gate and no claim here is made against a ceiling. tools/smoke_renderer.mjs holds the ceilings and remains the gate. What a reading of this shape can say is which of two tilings spends fewer triangles for how many more draw calls, measured the same way at the same stands in the same minute, and that is the only thing it is used for.

field.note: The spans are the ground MESH's bounding box, which is what tileGround() cuts and is therefore what the rule is asked about. It is the modelled box plus the skirt apron on all four sides (margin 2,659.84 m, data/terrain/epochs/e1834_harbor_cut/heightfield.json), which is why it is nearer square than the modelled box is.

rule.statement: Spend a fixed tile BUDGET on whatever shape the ground is. With r the box's long-to-short ratio, the long axis takes round(sqrt(budget * r^1.5)) cuts and the short axis takes round(budget / that). The exponent is the BEARING BIAS the 12 x 3 measurement was made at -- it spent a 2.525:1 box at 4:1, and ln 4 / ln 2.525 = 1.4965 -- written so that it vanishes on a square box instead of privileging east-west for no reason.
rule.reproduces_its_own_reading: groundTileGrid(2020, 800) === {cols: 12, rows: 3}, the grid the budget was measured at

budget.note: main.js BUDGET; the draw-call figure is the one the candidates are held to here.

chosen.why: It spends 76,121 fewer triangles than the literals it replaces at the worst stand, for one more draw call out of 215. 12 x 12 spends 58,287 fewer again and costs fifteen more calls, and 6 x 16 is worse than `derived` on both counts -- so the extra tiles are not bought. The point of the change is not the 76,121 anyway: it is that the grid now follows the box, and the box is going to move again.

stands.downtown: the four anchors tools/smoke_renderer.mjs owns, copied the way measure_detail_ceilings.mjs copies them
stands.south: four poses in local ENU metres down the new field -- 700 m, 1,800 m and 3,200 m south of the datum and one aerial over it. They are poses and not anchors because there are no anchors south of the town yet; that is T-0467. A tiling measured only downtown would be measured on the quarter of the box that did not change.

a_finding_this_is_not_the_ticket_for: THE SOUTHERN STANDS STAND WELL OVER THE SCENE-DETAIL CEILINGS, and no tiling moves that. At the `light` tier -- the floor, ceiling 825,000 triangles -- the worst southern stand reads 1,387,934 on the committed rule, because from 1.8 km south of the town the WHOLE town is in the frustum at once and nothing has ever measured a stand there. That is the buildings and the flora, not the ground: the ground is what this ticket tiled, and tiling it better took triangles OFF every one of those readings. Filed as its own ticket rather than folded in here.
